title: Polynomial action relations reduce coefficients to the base ring
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and let S be an R-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], generated by elements x_1, ..., x_n. Let N be an S-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] generated by e_1, ..., e_m subject to relations x_i e_j = sum_k a_{ijk} e_k with a_{ijk} in R. Then every element of N is an R-linear combination of e_1, ..., e_m.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0561, proof: the paragraph beginning “Suppose z = \sum b_j y_j” and its degree-lowering induction

proof.text: Let P be the R-submodule spanned by the specified e_j. For a generator x_i and v in P, use Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun to write v as a finite sum of R multiples of the e_j. Distribute x_i over that sum, commute its action with the R coefficients using the scalar tower, and substitute the action relations. Each resulting term lies in P, hence x_i preserves P.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0561, proof: the paragraph beginning “Suppose z = \sum b_j y_j” and its degree-lowering induction

proof.text: For s in the R-subalgebra generated by the x_i, prove that s preserves P by Algebra.adjoin_induction. The generator case is Step 1. Algebra-map scalars preserve the R-submodule P by IsScalarTower.algebraMap_smul. A sum of preserving scalars preserves P by add_smul and add_mem; a product does so by mul_smul and composition. Since the x_i generate S, every s in S preserves P.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0561, proof: the paragraph beginning “Suppose z = \sum b_j y_j” and its degree-lowering induction

proof.text: Every z lies in the S-span of the e_j by the specified generation hypothesis. Apply Submodule.span_induction: the e_j lie in P; zero and sums stay in P; and S-scalar multiples stay in P by Step 2. Thus z lies in P. Finally Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun gives coefficients c_j in R with sum_j c_j e_j = z; reverse the equality. No nonempty generating family or nontrivial ring is required.
